## Verified behavior and reasoning

The toolchain exporter requests the run and original artifact metadata through an authenticated GitHub API connection; verifies same repository, main push, completed P003/P004 workflow, run identity, publication commit, one unexpired expected toolchain artifact, finite integer size bounded at 1 GiB, and SHA-256 metadata; then downloads the original ZIP. It refuses an overlong body while reading and rejects truncated or altered bytes before creating the destination. It emits exact byte ranges, each no larger than 256 MiB, and an index with whole-archive and per-part hashes. It never unzips/rebuilds the original archive. Four parts cover its maximum accepted archive size. The index explicitly makes no phase-acceptance claim.

The failed-packaging reader requires a completed failed same-repository main-push Darling CI run. It queries all job attempts, binds each failed job to the run and head SHA, and preserves each original response byte in a gzip stream. Its raw hash, compressed hash, byte counts, and attempt identity are independently usable. Display excerpts are limited to the last 100 error matches and last 60 lines, with 4096-character truncation explicitly marked; the complete gzip content remains untruncated. A report cannot be completed if a selected download fails. Existing destination files are not overwritten.

Both workflows execute trusted main code with read-only contents/actions permissions and checkout credentials disabled. Untrusted originating run content is not executed by these readers. API tokens are attached only to GitHub API requests. The shared redirect handler rejects HTTP redirects and removes Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, and Cookie across origins. Once removed, credentials do not reappear if a later redirect returns to the API host.

### Original failure independently verified

Queried authenticated GitHub API metadata for readback run `42331833518`, artifact `13558056344`, and compared the local original ZIP: 15,099,347 bytes, SHA-256 `ae6ceaf869ad172204672076ffb60972ca5c026afd655dbc958120a0cec86d94`. ZIP CRC passed. The enclosed readback index matched the extracted index. Independently verified both the compressed binary-job log hash/size and decompressed original bytes: job `128255469767`, original run `42323661071`, source `3ecbd5bbb5e173ab74c2f2db236744b2fc81de69`, 97,987,499 raw bytes, 804,001 lines, SHA-256 `6239dda234c1909f1bb028decf8b97923570ff5999704bb08d8febc3b768d9ef`.

Original lines 803018–803024 show `dh_strip` invoking native `strip` on the text rule file `usr/libexec/darling/usr/share/file/magic/elf`, which fails with an unrecognized file format and aborts packaging. This identifies the failing packaging operation directly from the original job; it is not a guessed compiler failure.

### Reproduction without a classifier shim

The implementation tests use a controlled observed `file(1)` description so the regression can run on older Ubuntu hosts. The independent reviewer probe removed that shim entirely and used installed **file 5.46**, actual **dh_strip 13.24.2**, actual native **strip**, and actual pinned upstream magic bytes.

Independently queried the public GitHub tree at the repository's submodule pin `darlinghq/darling-file@c6ee65265d253d24b1a496f8ca54b5e449fe108c`. Its `file/magic/Magdir/elf` entry is blob `f5e1af9a25bc47f43016763c6d739f67b0d5c164`, 11,148 bytes. Local fixture bytes matched that Git blob and SHA-256 `ee93154f71cf3b9e1ce8f105d8ef8b9f5b04653502d867fd3a3d1cf310a9860d`.

Real file(1) classified those text bytes with the words “ELF executables.” The unchanged dh_strip path reproduced the format failure (exit 255). The actual repaired repository `make -f debian/rules override_dh_strip` target succeeded (exit 0), preserved all magic bytes, removed `.debug_info` from a separately compiled native ELF, and that executable still ran successfully.

The exclusion is confined to the magic text-data directory. It preserves native ELF stripping elsewhere and does not change compiler, runner, or real packaging requirements. Mandatory P003 fixture/P004 source jobs explicitly install debhelper for these tests.
